solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pointed tool held by smaller criminal

indicators.note: a thing held by another sits within its grasp, so the tool goes inside the word for smaller

parts.note: smaller means less
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing leather

explanation.surface: A sharp implement is clutched by a shorter crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone criminal acts outside the law, the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Certainly dismayed, in part

indicators.note: only a part of the word dismayed is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone is definitely upset, at least to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye is an old or dialect word of assent, like saying 'certainly' or 'yes'.

clue.text: Ignited high explosive, showing flexibility

parts.note: ignited means lit, set on fire

explanation.surface: Lighting a bomb is pictured as a sign of being supple.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithe body is supple and bends easily, so it shows flexibility.

clue.text: Difficulty with speech, failing Turing test?

indicators.note: the words Turing test are failing, breaking down into a new order

explanation.surface: A machine that fails the Turing test is imagined as having trouble talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The Turing test asks whether a machine's conversation can pass for human, so a speech problem fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stammer, repeating sounds involuntarily, is a well-known speech difficulty.

clue.text: Huts remodelled like this

indicators.note: huts that are remodelled are rebuilt in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some sheds have been rebuilt in the manner shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus is an adverb meaning in this way or like this.

clue.text: Drug English star

parts.note: heroin is an opiate drug

explanation.surface: A narcotic is described as a British celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The female lead of a film or novel is its star, its central character.

clue.text: Absorbing nitrogen, censures nasty skin lotion

indicators.note: something absorbing another takes it into itself, so the gas symbol goes inside
nasty suggests the word censures is messed up and rearranged

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A cream soaks up a gas while someone harshly criticises it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' scrambles CENSURES into SUSCREEN, and 'Absorbing' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunscreen is a lotion spread on the skin to block ultraviolet rays.

clue.text: Loudly sing opinion of unfashionable waistband?

definitions.meaning: to sing a song with great force and volume
a verdict on a belt that has gone out of style: that belt is out

explanation.surface: A singer gives a verdict on outdated fashion while bellowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as a fashion critic's two-word verdict: the belt is 'out', meaning no longer in style.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to sing or shout something very loudly and forcefully.

clue.text: Practical joke is quietly disgusting

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
rank means foul-smelling or disgusting

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a practical joke is secretly revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank is a trick played on someone for fun, a practical joke.

clue.text: Eater 'aving bananas (or nuts)?

indicators.note: bananas and nuts are both slang for crazy, so either tells us to jumble the letters

explanation.surface: A Cockney diner, dropping the h of 'having', is eating bananas or nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aving drops its h as in Cockney speech. Either 'bananas' or 'nuts' signals the anagram; read plainly, the whole clue describes someone who eats no meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives on fruit and nuts rather than meat follows a plant-based diet.

clue.text: Be painfully affected by belt-tightening?

parts.note: literally, a belt pulled too tight squeezes the waist; figuratively, belt-tightening means cutting spending, which hurts

explanation.surface: Someone suffers from a belt done up too tight.
explanation.walkthrough: Belt-tightening is the idiom for economising, so the hurt is financial as well as physical.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to suffer hardship from having less money than before.

clue.text: Tried catching tuna, say, around vessel supplied

indicators.note: the word for tried catching fish goes around the vessel, wrapping it

parts.note: tuna is an example of fish, so trying to catch it is to have fished
an urn is a vase or vessel

explanation.surface: An angler went after tuna near a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat in this fishing scene, but it is an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnished room or house has been supplied with furniture.

clue.text: Concerned with short Welsh dog going around shopkeeper

indicators.note: turning around means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: a short word is cut, so the dog's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the corgi is a breed of dog from Wales

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a stubby Welsh dog wandering around a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the dog's last letter, and 'going around' turns the whole combination back to front; the corgi is a short-legged breed, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer keeps a shop selling food and household goods.

clue.text: Remover of dirt or carbon with less fat

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
leaner meat has less fat

explanation.surface: Choosing between a dirt remover or a less fatty carbon product.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaner is a person or substance that removes dirt.

clue.text: Heard someone leaving Devonian town

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is spoken and we want its sound

parts.note: someone who exits could be called an exiter

explanation.surface: News got about that someone left a town in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; Exeter is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the cathedral city and main town of the county of Devon.

clue.text: US news magazine with a profit repeatedly

parts.note: Time is a long-running American news weekly
and means with, joining things
gain means profit

explanation.surface: An American news weekly turns a profit, over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for again and again, on many occasions.

clue.text: Sailor supporting a Liberal place of worship

indicators.note: in a down answer, a word supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman backs a Liberal candidate at church.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the holy table at the centre of worship in a church or temple.

clue.text: Peevish complaint from Caucasian changing time to noon

indicators.note: changing one thing to another swaps a letter in the word for Caucasian

parts.note: Caucasian is used to mean white-skinned

explanation.surface: A white person moans while altering the clock from one time to midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A whine is a querulous, petulant grumble.

clue.text: The man's Conservative past

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician's earlier career as a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's history is their record or what lies in the past.

clue.text: Left-wing Republican editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor who is a Republican yet left-leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the colour of socialism and communism, so it means left-wing.

clue.text: Departs with ship full of animals that's not light

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables
Noah's ark carried the animals two by two

explanation.surface: A boat crammed with creatures sets off in the gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark is the opposite of light, with little or no brightness.

clue.text: Disorderly nit, impolite to enter uninvited

indicators.note: disorderly means out of order, so the letters of nit are rearranged

parts.note: rude means impolite

explanation.surface: A rowdy, ill-mannered fool barges in uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to come in where one is not welcome or invited.
